key_insight: OpenForgeRL makes it possible to train agent systems that use real inference harnesses, not just simplified prompt loops. In simple terms, it bridges the gap between powerful multi-turn agent runtimes and open-source SFT/RL training stacks.
problem_solved: Existing open infrastructure struggles to train stateful, multi-process, harness-driven agents end-to-end because standard SFT/RL pipelines cannot naturally represent complex inference workflows like tool use, external system access, and multi-step reasoning.
method: Provides an open-source framework for end-to-end training of harness-based agents.
Supports stateful, multi-process inference patterns used by modern agent harnesses.
Enables training across diverse environments while preserving the structure of real agent execution.
impact: This matters because practitioners can now train agents in setups that more closely match deployment-time behavior, reducing the gap between research prototypes and real-world systems. It also lowers dependence on closed training stacks for advanced agent workflows.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing standard RL/SFT vs. harness-native training
Architecture diagram of an agent loop with reasoning, tools, and external systems
Workflow graphic illustrating multi-turn, stateful harness execution
Icons for training, environment interaction, and tool use
paper_title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
paper_authors: Xiao Yu, Baolin Peng, Ruize Xu, Hao Zou, Qianhui Wu
